newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht eases on dollar gains.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht eases on dollar gains.

text.p: * Thai baht eases on dollar's overnight gains versus majors. Positive economic data underpins currency, keeping it below central bank's mid-rate.
* Singapore dollar remains soft but subdued after overnight sales on news of Brunei finance minister's resignation.
* Malaysian ringgit under pressure from dollar's rise.
* Indonesian rupiah driven by liquidity conditions.

The Thai baht subsided in line with the dollar's overnight gains versus the majors following comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan suggesting a U.S. interest rate hike might be in the offing.
The baht was quoted at 25.893-25.898 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 25.842/25.852 late on Wednesday.
But dealers said it remained below the central bank's daily fixing of 25.91 for most of Thursday's morning session after the Finance Ministry leaked relatively positive economic data on Wednesday.

"I believe the baht is now returning to its normal footing, tracking the dollar/majors. The data yesterday might be viewed by some as still depressing. But if you put it into context, it showed a positive trend," said a UK bank dealer in Bangkok.
The data showed Thailand's December trade deficit narrowed to 22.3 billion baht from 24.2 billion baht in November.
The Finance Ministry said exports growth for 1996 contracted 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent contraction forecast by the Bank of Thailand earlier.
An SBC Warburg analyst said the chance that investors might be moved into a baht selling spree again was minimal after the ministry's release of the data.
The central bank is due to officialy release its key economic indicators on Thursday at 0800 GMT.

"I see this as an improvement. Of course, some investors might want to see the trade deficit narrow because of strong improvement in exports rather than of the substantial drop in imports. But at the end of the day, it is the trade balance figure that affects the currency." he said.
"And I don't think any speculator who recently took losses from the Bank of Thailand's intervention will have more risk appetite to speculate on baht devaluation again soon," he said.
Elsewhere, the Singapore dollar remained under pressure after reaching an overnight low of 1.4280 to the U.S. dollar.
Dealers said funds had sold the Sing dollar following news that Brunei's Finance Minister had resigned and been replaced by his brother, the Sultan of the tiny oil kingdom.
The news spurred speculation Brunei might want to weaken its currency or de-link it from the Singapore dollar, dealers said.
"There were rumours Brunei wanted to bring up its non-oil exports. One way to do that would be to weaken the Brunei dollar, which is pegged against the Sing dollar," said a local bank dealer.

He said there was some buying of dollar/Sing by interbank players in the morning but it looked capped near its overnight highs. "There's no real interest from customers. They're probably all speculative buys," he said.
Dealers said the dollar/Sing was likely to trade a 1.4240-1.4290 range for the day. It was quoted at 1.4267/77 at 0405 GMT.
In Malaysia, the ringgit remained under pressure from the dollar's overnight rise but dealers said strong dollar selling interest around the 2.4925 level would limit the ringgit's fall.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4833/43 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 2.4810/20 at its Kuala Lumpur close on Wednesday.
"Dollar/ringgit's looking biddish after last night. But it'll probably trade a 2.4840-2.4900 range today," said a Singapore-based dealer.
The Indonesian rupiah was easier as the market continued to focus on liquidity conditions in the absence of other leads.
Spot rupiah was at 2,391.5/92.0 at 0405 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,391.0/92.0.
Dealers said short-term swaps fell, while longer-term rates were stable, suggesting the temporary nature of the current ample conditions.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,381/2,573 and the conversion band 2,381/2,429 on Wednesday after raising them by one point on Tuesday.
-- Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anchalee Koetsawang (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
